sentences.text: No; at the time of reset of interest rates, the lender may, at its option, provide borrowers a choice to switch to a fixed rate as per its Board-approved policy, so the option is permitted rather than mandatory.
For EMI-based personal loans, the in-force reset rule uses the same permissive wording, stating that the RE may, at its option, provide a choice to switch over to a fixed rate.
The bank’s own policy also says it may, at its option, offer the borrower a choice to switch to a fixed rate at the time of reset of the floating rate.
